title: How useful is a lookup-heavy small backbone?
question: How useful is a lookup-heavy small backbone across declared lexical table capacities?
hypothesis: Larger lexical tables may alter endpoint recall while exposing wording, collision, and override failures.
failure_interpretation: Lookup may overfit exact wording, collide, or fail chat, paraphrase, and override checks even if it improves a lookup-sensitive score.
controls: Fix tokenizer, dataset source and packing within each selected data route.
Fix seed-matched model width, depth, heads, optimizer, runtime, budget, evaluator, and endpoint policy unless a listed axis changes.
Report held-out language-model loss separately from each capability card category.
confounders: Model-construction RNG changes when module inventories differ.
Approximate scale classes rather than matched parameter counts.
Educational-kernel overhead is not an architecture-speed measurement.
hardware_notes: Inspect table bytes before tiny; this fixed-neural table sweep is not an iso-total allocation curve.
runtime_class: Qualitative scale-dependent educational PyTorch workload; measure local runtime rather than inferring timing.

can_establish: Observed table-capacity endpoint contrasts with fixed reduced neural backbone per selected scale.
cannot_establish: An iso-total allocation curve, semantic retrieval result, code/API/formula/composition evidence, speed claim, or cross-tokenizer equivalence.
